title: Personalized Intervention Group (PING): A Proof-of-Concept Study of a Network-Informed, Personalized Approach to Bridging Waiting Times for Psychotherapy
summary:
Many children and adolescents experience psychological distress such as low mood, strong worries, or problems with anger and aggression. Although many of them need support, they often have to wait several months for a place in psychotherapy. During this waiting period, symptoms can worsen. Therefore, support programs are needed to help children and adolescents during this time.

This study examines whether a group program can help bridge the waiting time for a psychotherapy place. A new approach will be tested that assumes different problems are connected and can influence each other. For example, sleep problems may lead adolescents to feel exhausted, withdraw from others, and experience a further decline in mood. These connections are represented in so-called person-specific networks, which can serve as a basis for therapy decisions. At the beginning of the study, the individual relationships between different problems experienced by the adolescents are therefore assessed, for example how sleep problems, worries, or social withdrawal are related to one another. Based on this information, topics for the group sessions are selected that best match the personal difficulties of the participants.

The study will include 40 adolescents aged twelve to seventeen who are on the waiting list for outpatient psychotherapy at the Psychological Outpatient Clinic for Children and Adolescents at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz. Some adolescents will start the group intervention immediately, while others will first wait six to ten weeks and then also take part in the group. This design makes it possible to examine whether changes in symptoms are greater during participation in the group than during the waiting period.

The groups consist of several sessions in which the adolescents’ personal difficulties, such as distressing thoughts, feelings, and behaviors, are addressed. During the study, participants complete several questionnaires about their mood, worries, behavior, and quality of life. They are also asked how helpful and understandable they find the personalized approach. The aim of the study is to examine whether this new approach is feasible in everyday practice, is accepted by adolescents, and provides initial indications of positive effects.
conditions: It concerns adolescents who present for outpatient psychotherapy. Following an initial intake session, a suspected diagnosis according to ICD-10 is established. The intervention is delivered transdiagnostically, meaning it is not restricted to a specific disorder category.

interventions.name: Arm 1: Network-informed modularized personalized group psychotherapy; selection of treatment targets based on person-specific symptom networks; delivery of six modules with personalized content based on the identified treatment targets.

Arm 2: Initially passive control group, creation of personalized symptom networks and placement on a waiting list for the intervention to be delivered later. After the waiting period, implementation of the personalized group intervention.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion is transdiagnostic, meaning that participants are included regardless of the (suspected) specific disorder, provided that an indication for outpatient psychotherapy has been established during an initial intake session. Additional inclusion criteria are sufficient German language proficiency and written informed consent from the participants and from their legal guardians.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients are excluded if they present with acute suicidality or other crisis states requiring immediate treatment, manifest psychotic disorders, or severe intellectual disability, as well as significant cognitive or language impairments that would make participation in the assessments impossible.
